method: AI-assisted metadata/abstract review; not human or librarian validated. No live retrieval or full-text reading was performed by this reviewer.

rubric.direct: Captured evidence supports the material topic facets and explicit format, method, and date requirements; record identity suffices for exact-work requests. Topic-level relevance may be supported by an unambiguous title for broad questions.
rubric.supporting: Useful context or partial fit, including records whose truncated excerpt does not establish a required facet or method. This is not a finding that the full work necessarily fails the request.
rubric.unsuitable: Evidence contradicts a material requested format, event, or purpose; off-topic or inappropriate for the specified task.
rubric.uncertain: Insufficient captured evidence to decide even contextual usefulness for the requested question.

limitations: Many captured abstracts stop after about 300 characters and may omit methods, geographic details, or findings. Direct-match counts are conservative and not an estimate of scholarly truth or full-text accuracy.
Provider peer-review flags are reported evidence only. Neither peer-review practices nor methodological quality was independently checked.
No judgments assert that an AI-generated claim is correct; source relevance and bibliographic existence differ from claim accuracy.
Supporting records in exact-item queries are distinct related readings, not additional exact matches. Probable duplicate manifestations are flagged separately.
No original capture judgments or human-review fields were modified. A faculty/librarian review is still required.

concerns.finding: Government hearings occupy the first two positions for an introductory-book request. Record-format normalization or ranking is too permissive.
The returned records do not establish contemporaneous Greensboro primary evidence; a Wichita oral history is a different event and the second interview lacks usable descriptive metadata.
A newspaper review of a historical novel ranks first; the other result is an academic book review, so the search supplies no confirmed historical study in the top results.
The correct original ranks first, but two Vogel chapter manifestations appear potentially duplicated. Verify by publisher DOI/ISBN; normalized title and date alone miss this case.

All five results are promising qualitative topic matches, but the capture truncates before interview methods. Evaluation should retain fuller method excerpts or full abstracts before claiming method accuracy.
These five cases returned no sources in this half. Missing provider configuration and narrow-query coverage require separate diagnosis; no-source output is not a negative literature finding.

recommendations: Enforce requested document kinds before treating catalog records as matching books; distinguish monographs from government hearings and book reviews.
For history, assess the relationship of a primary artifact to the event and time period rather than assuming that a title keyword or an interview format establishes suitability.
Rank underlying books and historical scholarship above reviews and reviews of fiction for scholarly research requests.
Deduplicate title variants using DOI, ISBN, container, authors, and chapter metadata; preserve edition distinctions only when materially useful.
Retain enough abstract text for method assessment and label unknown methods as unknown instead of inferring interviews from qualitative.
Report this review as provisional AI-assisted relevance assessment and retain human review as a separate validation step.
